task.title: Regression: slugify keeps separator runs and edge hyphens
task.statement: Regression report for slugkit.slugify(text). Since the last change the function returns 'hello--world' for 'Hello--World', 'a---b' for 'a -- b' and 'end-' for 'end!'. The intended behaviour, which the existing tests only partly cover, is: lower-case the text; every maximal run of one or more characters that are not ASCII letters a-z or ASCII digits 0-9 becomes exactly one hyphen; leading and trailing hyphens are removed; an input with no ASCII letters or digits (including the empty string and whitespace-only text) returns ''. Non-ASCII letters such as 'é' are separators, not kept characters (so 'café crème' is 'caf-cr-me'). Keep raising TypeError for non-string input, keep returning a str, and keep the existing tests in tests/ passing without modifying them. Fix the regression in slugkit/core.py.
acceptance_criteria: slugify('Hello--World') == 'hello-world', slugify('a -- b') == 'a-b', slugify('one , two ; three') == 'one-two-three', slugify('x___y') == 'x-y' (runs of separators collapse to one hyphen).
slugify('end!') == 'end', slugify('  padded  ') == 'padded', slugify('--both--') == 'both', slugify('(parens)') == 'parens' (no leading or trailing hyphen).
slugify('') == '', slugify('!!!') == '', slugify('   ') == '' (nothing to keep gives the empty string).

Existing behaviour is preserved: slugify('Hello World') == 'hello-world', slugify('already-a-slug') == 'already-a-slug', slugify('Python 3') == 'python-3', slugify('MiXeD CaSe 42') == 'mixed-case-42'.
Non-ASCII letters are separators: slugify('café crème') == 'caf-cr-me' and slugify('日本語') == ''.
The result is a str; TypeError for non-string input such as None, 3, 2.5, ['a'] and b'bytes'.

interface_contract.name: slugkit.slugify
interface_contract.behavior: Accept a str, including str subclasses, and return a str. Apply Python str.lower() first. In the resulting text, retain only ASCII a-z and 0-9; replace each maximal nonempty run of other characters with exactly one ASCII hyphen, then remove all edge hyphens. Classification occurs after lowercasing, preserving the existing operation order; Unicode lowercase mappings that produce ASCII characters therefore retain those characters. Do not perform transliteration or Unicode normalization. The function remains available through both slugkit.slugify and slugkit.core.slugify.
error_cases: TypeError when text is not an instance of str, including None, 3, 2.5, ['a'], and b'bytes'; preserve the existing message 'text must be a str'.
TypeError for missing text or additional unsupported arguments, consistent with the signature.

acceptance_criteria: 1. Separator runs collapse: slugify('Hello--World') == 'hello-world', slugify('a -- b') == 'a-b', slugify('one , two ; three') == 'one-two-three', and slugify('x___y') == 'x-y'.
2. Edge separators disappear: slugify('end!') == 'end', slugify('  padded  ') == 'padded', slugify('--both--') == 'both', and slugify('(parens)') == 'parens'.
3. Empty or separator-only inputs return '': verify '', '!!!', '   ', '--', and '\t\n'.
4. Existing outputs remain unchanged: 'Hello World' becomes 'hello-world', 'already-a-slug' remains 'already-a-slug', 'Python 3' becomes 'python-3', and 'MiXeD CaSe 42' becomes 'mixed-case-42'.
5. Non-ASCII characters remaining after lowercasing are separators: slugify('café crème') == 'caf-cr-me', slugify('日本語') == '', and slugify('a１２b') == 'a-b'.
6. Lowercasing precedes ASCII classification: slugify('K') == 'k' and slugify('İ') == 'i', following Python str.lower() mappings without additional normalization.
7. ASCII letters and digits are preserved in order after lowercasing: slugify('ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789') == 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789'.
8. Mixed separator types form a single run: slugify('a \t\n_!é--b') == 'a-b'.
9. Every successful result is a str and is either empty or consists of nonempty ASCII lowercase alphanumeric groups separated by single hyphens, with no edge hyphens.
10. Each of None, 3, 2.5, ['a'], and b'bytes' raises TypeError with message 'text must be a str'; string subclass instances are accepted.
11. Both public import paths remain usable, and slugify(text='Hello World') returns 'hello-world'.
12. All existing tests in tests/ pass unchanged.

Changing the function signature, public import paths, or non-string input policy.
Adding transliteration, Unicode normalization, configurable separators, or dependencies.

Sealed and adversarial suites run one child process per test under a supervisor that never imports candidate code and is the first step of its branch; two verifier canaries detect blanket result forgery. A candidate can still forge its own result from inside a child after the nonce was read if it spares the canaries (the mutation gate and held-out tests are the structural detectors).

The repository's own suite and the held-out suite run after the sealed verification in their own branches. They are bound through the same supervisor only for unittest repositories whose tests are statically discoverable; otherwise they are parsed from console output and the gate is labelled evidence_class 'stdout'.

Model-written sealed and adversarial tests can be wrong; their failures block VERIFIED. An independent arbiter classifies each failure (implementation bug, test defect or contract dispute) and, for pure test defects, offers a corrected module. The correction counts only after mechanical validation (same test methods, only the failing ones changed, passes on the candidate, still fails on the unmodified base or is caught by a mutant); the corrected gate is then re-run and the verdict re-derived from the gates. A sealed test that failed by assertion or by an exception raised in the code under test is never overridden (only a test-internal crash or a timeout may be corrected). The classification itself remains a model judgement.

INFEASIBLE is recorded only when a witness program written by the contract auditor demonstrated the contradiction by running on the unmodified repository (exit code and output recorded); the witness's logic is the model's, its execution is not.
